body: The City of Cleveland has asked to join Fannie Mae's federal foreclosure case over Reserve Square, News 5 Cleveland reported. The motion to intervene was filed September 28, 2026 in Fannie Mae v. Reserve Apartments, Ltd., No. 1:25-cv-01510 in the Northern District of Ohio, before Judge Bridget Meehan Brennan, according to the docket. The city says the property is a public nuisance and that the receiver is not doing enough about 19 open violation notices covering dozens of issues, including elevator outages, water damage and parking-garage deterioration. "We were patient for a long time," Law Director Mark Griffin told News 5, adding that the city "felt that we had to step in." It wants every violation fixed, the current owner held accountable and future owners kept from neglecting the building. A city spokesman said demolition is not being considered at this time.

Reserve Square covers a downtown block off East 12th Street between Chester and Superior avenues, with 975 apartments in two 1970s towers, a garage of nearly 1,000 spaces and about 220,000 square feet of commercial space, News 5 reported. It is about 80% vacant. Fannie Mae began the foreclosure in July 2025 over more than $78 million in unpaid principal, interest and fees, and the owner, an affiliate of Willoughby-based K&D Group, cooperated; K&D's CEO blamed a vacancy surge tied to federal immigration policy changes and the loss of international students for making refinancing impossible. The Michigan-based Hayman Company took over as receiver in August 2025.

The docket shows the court entered an in rem judgment and judgment in mortgage foreclosure on consent on April 14, 2026, and later confirmed that the receivership remains in place. After a February 2026 letter of concern from the city, the court ordered the receiver to file weekly status reports. The receiver's reports describe removing squatters, treating bedbugs, new cleaning and security crews, and contractors working on water damage and elevators, according to News 5. The property is listed for sale with Institutional Property Advisors, part of Marcus & Millichap, with no asking price. The receiver did not respond to News 5's requests for comment.

timeline.label: Fannie Mae files foreclosure suit and an agreed motion to appoint a receiver
Court appoints the Hayman Company as receiver
After a letter from the City of Cleveland, the court orders the receiver to file weekly status reports
Court enters a consent in rem judgment and judgment in mortgage foreclosure; the receivership remains in place
City of Cleveland moves to intervene, citing 19 open code-violation notices
Court grants an extension of time to respond to the motion to intervene
